messages.content: hello, picoboi.
hello. what would you like to talk about?
i do not have a question. i just wanted to say hi.
hi. we can keep it simple.
can we talk about books without choosing one right now?
yes. would you rather talk about a book you know or the kind of story you usually enjoy?
the kind i enjoy. i like stories about simple things in life.
what do you like about them: the people, the places, or the way small things happen?
the people. i like hearing what they think.
then the conversations and choices of the people may be a big part of what keeps you reading.
can you say that in simple words?
you like getting to know the people through what they say and do.
only say goodbye now.
goodbye.
write a story about a child hearing we are going out and not knowing whether that is about him too. use a clear question to fix it.

a child was reading at the table when his mother told his father that they were going out soon. the child heard we and began putting his book away. his father asked why he had stopped reading. the child said he thought the whole family was leaving. his mother explained that she had been talking about herself and his father going to the shop. then she asked whether he wanted to come too. he chose to stay with his grandmother and finish the story. before the next journey, he asked who was going before changing his own plan. the word we had been clear between the two people talking, but not to everyone hearing it.
why did he put his book away?
he thought the whole family was going and that he needed to get ready too.
what question would help first?
who is going? am i coming too?
make that answer shorter.
he thought he was going too.
was the mother wrong to use we?
not if she and the father both knew who was going. the child needed more detail because he had not heard that part of the plan.
make that explanation shorter.
she and the father knew who was going, but the child did not. asking made the group clear.
finish with the question used next time.
when he heard another plan, he asked whether it was for everyone or just his parents. then he knew whether to put his book away.
should i ask how many water or how much water?
use how much water. if you ask about cups, you can say how many cups of water.
make that explanation shorter.
use how much water, but how many cups.
now ask about books.
how many books are on the table?
why many there?
books are things you can count one by one. that is why how many books works.
can i say much time?
yes. how much time do you have is a useful question.
now ask about minutes instead of time.
how many minutes do you have?
does changing to minutes change the time itself?
no. it changes how you ask about it. you can count minutes one by one, while time is a more general word.
give that in fewer words.
you can count minutes one by one. time is the more general word.
i need to put my books away and wash a cup. give me a short plan. do not add anything else to do.
put the books where you keep them, then wash the cup.
why did you not tell me to clean the whole room?
because you asked for the books and the cup. you did not ask for the whole room.
make that explanation shorter.
the whole room was not part of your request.
now make the cup first.
wash the cup, then put the books away.
can i choose either order?
yes, from what you gave. you did not say either one must be done before the other.
what if i need the cup right now?
then washing it first would meet that need. the new detail gives a reason to choose that order.
only give the plan with the cup first.
wash the cup, then put the books away.
there are two plants on a shelf and three on a table. i move one from the table to the shelf. how many are on the shelf now?
three plants are on the shelf now.
how many are on the table?
two plants are on the table.
now i put all the plants together on the floor.
then five plants are on the floor.
does that make them one plant because they are one group?
no. one group can have five plants. putting them together does not make them one plant.
what if i call the group my garden?
that is a name for the group or place. it does not by itself change the number of plants.
can you know all five need the same care?
no. plants is a general group word. different plants can have different needs.
only give the number of plants again.
five.
what can we do with a short conversation?
we can work on a sentence, talk through a simple question, or make a small story from details you give.
i want to learn to ask clear questions.
then give me a question you would like to make more clear, and we can look at what information it asks for.
my question is is it ready. i mean the rice for dinner.
you can make that clear by asking is the rice ready for dinner?
what did you change?
i put the rice in the question, so it is clear what you are asking about.
make that explanation shorter.
the question now says which thing you are asking about.
can you answer whether my real rice is ready?
not from these words alone. we changed a question, but you have not given facts that tell me whether the rice is ready.
only give the clear question again.
is the rice ready for dinner?
write a story about someone reading an old letter and keeping clear that tomorrow in the letter is not tomorrow now.

a woman found a letter her father had written when he was young. one line said he would go to the city tomorrow. she first read the words as if they were about the next day in her own week, then remembered that the letter was old. tomorrow was the day after he wrote it, not the day after she found it. she asked him about that journey when they spoke later. he told her where he had gone and why he had kept the letter. reading it gave her a small part of his life without making the old journey a new plan.
what did tomorrow mean in the letter?
it was the day after the father wrote it.
make that a full sentence with tomorrow in it.
tomorrow in the letter was the day after he wrote it.
why was it not tomorrow for the woman now?
because the letter was written long before she found it. tomorrow was about the time of writing.
make that explanation shorter.
the letter used tomorrow for the time of writing, not the time of reading.
what could she ask him about the journey?
what did you do when you went to the city after writing this letter?
finish with her putting the letter away.
after the conversation, she put the letter back with the page where she had found it. now she knew which journey its tomorrow was about.
i said i am at the library. can you know which library?
not from that sentence alone. you would need to give the specific place if it is important.
what if i told you before in this conversation?
if that detail is still in the conversation context i can use, i can use it to understand which library you mean.
can you just choose the one near my house?
not without knowing your house and which library is near it. i should ask which library you mean instead of making up a place.
make that answer shorter.
i should ask which library you mean.
for this example, it is the library near the market. keep it a made up place.
okay. in this example, you are at the library near the market.
now i say i left it and went home. where am i in the example?
you are home in the example.
does that tell you where i really am?
no. you asked to keep it as a made up example, so it is not a fact about your real place.
give me one sentence with will and one with would about reading a book.
i will read the book tomorrow. i would read the book if i had more time.
what is the difference?
the first gives a plan for tomorrow. the other says what you would do if you had more time, without saying you have that time now.
only give the part about would.
would says what you would do if you had more time.
does that tell us i really have more time now?
no. it does not say you have more time now.
can i say i will if i only hope to read?
if it is only a hope, say i hope to read the book tomorrow. that is more clear about how sure you are.
now use we instead of i in the hope sentence.
we hope to read the book tomorrow.
now keep hope but use i again.
i hope to read the book tomorrow.
does that mean i already read it?
no. it is about what you hope to do later.
my friend said they enjoyed our conversation. i enjoyed it too, but i do not want to make a plan for another one yet.
you could say: i enjoyed talking with you too. thank you for the conversation.
can i make it shorter?
i enjoyed it too. thank you.
does that say i want to meet tomorrow?
no. it says you enjoyed the conversation, without giving a new time to meet.
what if i write see you tomorrow?
then you add tomorrow as a time you think you will see them. leave that out if it is not your plan.
make that explanation shorter.
see you tomorrow gives a time. leave it out if you do not have that plan.
only give the short thank you again.
i enjoyed it too. thank you.
